findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: _BOOKKEEPING now fullmatches command.strip(); the newline form returns gate and the hook exits 2 (CASES row plus the bypass list), while the workflow's one-line command stays exempt.
findings.message: The exemption is checked against whitespace-flattened text, so `git commit -q -m "chore(T-1): task manifest" --<newline>.aegis/runs/T-1` counts as exempt (the hook exits 0), but bash runs a commit with no pathspec. Verified: a staged src/evil.py was committed with no gate.
findings.minimal_fix: Fullmatch against the raw command with only backslash-newlines folded; the workflow's one-line command still matches.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: Branching on 'R'/'C' in record[:2] puts src/c.py back in scope with no bogus /c.py for status RD (probed).
findings.message: Only `R `, `RM` and ` R` consume the source record, so a rename in state RD or RT (`git mv src/c.py src/c2.py && rm src/c2.py`) drops src/c.py from scope and adds a bogus `/c.py`. The deletion never reaches the lens diff or trace.
findings.minimal_fix: Branch on 'R' in record[:2] / 'C' in record[:2] instead of listing XY pairs.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: All three spellings now gate: any -c/--config-env alias.*, and a shell invoked by path through _SHELL_STRING (probed).
findings.message: Inline aliases `git -c alias.ci='!git commit' ci -am x` and `X=commit git --config-env=alias.ci=X ci -am x` both return none, and both commit (verified); so does `/bin/bash -c "git commit -am x"`. None of the three runs the gate.
findings.minimal_fix: Gate any -c/--config-env alias.* definition whatever its value; allow a path before sh/bash in _SHELL_STRING.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: checks.expired() compares parsed dates and core._valid_date enforces the YYYY-MM-DD shape, so 20260101 and 2026-W01-1 now read as expired and fail validation (probed); waiver_for, apply_waivers and _dismissal_problems all use it.
findings.message: Waiver expiry is a string compare, but the schema's date check (date.fromisoformat, Python 3.11+) also accepts `20260101` and `2026-W01-1`, and both sort as unexpired on 2026-09-17 (verified). A dismissal dated that way never expires within its year.
findings.minimal_fix: Compare date.fromisoformat(w['expires']) >= date.today() here and in waiver_for.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: diff, log and staged_files read -z and the log adds --no-renames; a committed non-ASCII baselined file is in scope by its real name (probed).
findings.message: `git log --name-only` quotes non-ASCII paths and omits rename sources, so a baselined `legacy/résumé.py` that was committed and then reverted to its adoption bytes stays exempt (verified).

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: shopt -s nocasematch refuses .aegis/Answers.json, .AEGIS/answers.json and the generated/constitution variants (probed).
findings.message: The answers.json refusal matches case-sensitively, so on case-insensitive APFS a write to `.aegis/Answers.json` (same inode) exits 0.
findings.minimal_fix: shopt -s nocasematch before the case statement.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: The rename test now bases changed_files on the commit sha, which fails under the old parser (probed); a new RD test covers the deleted destination.
findings.message: This R-26 test passes without the rename-source change: with base None, the diff from the empty tree to HEAD already lists the committed src/auth.py. Restoring the old parser keeps it green (verified).
findings.minimal_fix: Assert on changed_files(ctx, <HEAD sha after the auth commit>).
